sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:48

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:48:1
items.html:
The Malchut of Tevuna is actual Malchut in relation to the generality of Bina and Tevuna together, etc., whereas the Malchut of Bina is the body of the generality: This means that the upper Ima and Tevuna are in truth the discernment of ten Sefirot in the relation of the Bina of direct light, the upper Ima being GAR [first three] and Tevuna being ZAT, except that they divided by force of the rise of the bottom Hey to the Einayim, as above at length. Therefore the Malchut of Tevuna is the Malchut of both of them, of Ima and of Tevuna together. But the Malchut of the upper AVI “is the discernment of the body of the generality, and it is the place of the Chazeh of the Tifferet of the generality of the Partzuf of Bina and Tevuna together, and it is not actual Malchut.” That is to say, afterward, in Atzilut, Tevuna clothes from the Chazeh downward of the upper Ima, and thus the place of the Chazeh is the discernment of the body of the generality of the two of them, and it is not Malchut.
And according to what has been explained above you will understand the matter thoroughly. For it was explained that the upper Ima expands only until Hod, but she has no Yesod, as written above (page 522, the passage beginning “Tifferet”). The reason is that the Hassadim ceased there, and there is nothing there except the illumination of Hochma without Hassadim, which is not of the discernment of Ima at all, since she is the very opposite, the discernment of Hassadim without Hochma. Therefore the upper AVI were drawn only as far as the coupling of the screen of phase one, where there is at least still light of Hassadim; but after the screen of phase one refined, their illumination ceased entirely, for she has no expansion whatsoever without Hassadim, and the level of Malchut was unable to come out with the upper AVI. Only with YESHSUT, after it had separated into a Partzuf of its own, was the level of Malchut able to come out without the illumination of Hassadim, as explained.
